quote: Oh, we can definitely help you out. 700?
stewart_read: Rep captures a strong $700/month anchor but reacts with a flat acknowledgment instead of flipping it into alignment against the utility.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately saving the flip for the specialist call, but nothing in the transcript signals this was planned rather than just moving on.
coaching_implication: Suggested rephrase: 'So Dominion's charging you $700 just to keep the lights on — that's exactly the number our specialist will show you how to erase.' Ties the pain to action.

quote: a couple of people on my block didn't get them put in
stewart_read: Customer offers unsolicited neighbor/social-proof context; rep does not probe which neighbors or what happened.
coaching_implication: A quick follow-up ('oh yeah? did you see what they got?') builds curiosity cheaply and costs nothing.

quote: a lot of people on my block been lately getting it put in
stewart_read: Second mention of the same neighbor signal in the same breath, again unprobed.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch of the same missed hook — reinforces it as a pattern, not a one-off.

quote: And you have a credit score over 670. Right?
stewart_read: Customer answers 'not sure,' rep logs it and moves on without treating it as a hard gate or offering reassurance about the closer verifying it.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive — rep should have briefly reassured ('no worries, our specialist will confirm that') rather than silently noting uncertainty.
coaching_implication: A one-line reassurance here reduces anxiety about disqualification before the appointment.

quote: Because the, the light bill is actually in my daughter's name.
stewart_read: Customer discloses the utility account is in someone else's name — a potential co-owner/decision-maker signal — and rep only reacts with surprise, no follow-up on whether the daughter is on title or needs to be involved.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as irrelevant since co-owner was already confirmed 'no' earlier, but the daughter's name on the bill raises a legitimate question about who else has a stake.
coaching_implication: Should have asked whether the daughter lives there or needs to be part of the appointment given her name is on the account.

stewart_read: Customer's confusion about what the appointment covers reveals the button-up expectations weren't set before this point in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive gap — the rep answers well when asked but never proactively explains the appointment's purpose before the customer had to ask.
coaching_implication: Set expectations once, clearly, before offering times: 'this appointment is where we show you the numbers, not install anything.'

quote: When he had discussed the about how much it'll be.
stewart_read: Even after booking and a recap, the customer is still asking what the appointment covers — no 'is that fair?' handshake was used to confirm understanding before closing.
coaching_implication: Add the verbal handshake after the recap to catch lingering confusion before hanging up.
